properties.title: Olivine Abundance · Kaguya SP North Polar 50-90N (Lemelin et al. 2022)
properties.authors: Myriam Lemelin, Paul G. Lucey, Alex Camon
properties.crs: Source: Moon_2000_Stereographic_North_Pole (1737400 m sphere, true scale at the pole), georeferenced only by corner GCPs in the .aux.xml sidecar, rows stored bottom-up. COG: IAU:30130, north-up, same grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Kaguya Spectral Profiler reflectance, gridded, interpolated and scaled to LRO LOLA 1064 nm reflectance; mineral abundance modeled as described in Lemelin et al. (2022), section 3.4. Distributed on Zenodo as a Float32 GeoTIFF in weight fraction with Esri sidecars. COG: gdal_translate assigns IAU:30130 and the bottom-up geotransform given by the GCP corners (+/-1267472 m); gdal_calc.py multiplies values by 100 to wt%; gdalwarp with nearest neighbor onto the identical extent and size flips rows to north-up with pixel values unchanged, and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Olivine abundance at 1 km/pixel for the north polar region (50-90N). Olivine-rich exposures in crater central peaks and basin rings are candidate deep-crust or upper-mantle material (Lemelin et al. 2015, 2019).
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Spectral Profiler mineral model at 1 km/pixel, 50-90N. No NoData value; pixels outside the mapped circle are 0 in all four mineral maps.
properties.lri:quality_note: The raster has no NoData value. Inside the mapped circle (data reach 49.9 deg latitude) the four SP mineral maps sum to exactly 100 wt% at every pixel, so 0 is a zero abundance there; 55.0% of pixels poleward of 50 deg are 0 in this map. Outside the circle all four maps are 0 as fill. Source values are weight fraction (maximum 0.76); the COG stores wt%. Source rows are stored bottom-up and georeferenced only by GCPs; the COG is north-up. Along the 49.9-50 deg boundary ring the mean is 2.7 wt% here and 4.3 wt% in the Kaguya MI 50N-50S map (correlation 0.49), so the two products do not join seamlessly.
